items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: In fact, Charlie Dixon was more of a father to the band. Everybody looked up at Charlie Dixon as an advisor. And he was exceptionally crazy about me. He used to call me Big Jim.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. I see. So some of the guys would be faking, but the others would read their parts. That's right. And not, you didn't try to make it anything special, just like it was written. I see. What happened to Charlie Dixon?

Charlie Dixon passed about three or five years ago. He died in San Antonio, Texas. He was a wonderful musician and a great fellow. In fact, Charlie Dixon was more of a father to the band. Everybody looked up at Charlie Dixon as an advisor. And he was exceptionally crazy about me. He used to call me Big Jim. Why, I don't know, but that's what he, Monarchy, laid on me.
I wondered about that band. A whole lot of things, you know. He seemed to have a quite unusual style. I never heard anybody else play trombone quite like Charlie Dixon.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: Charlie Dixon was one of the greatest men that I've met in my life.

ctx.x: Now what about, uh, Charlie Dixon? Who all did they, they were.

Charlie Dixon was one of the greatest men that I've met in my life. I wouldn't say he was the greatest musician, but he was truly a great man. And by the same token, he could play his bass and he could play his punk. He played with Singers Smith, which was another band that I didn't know, but Brad's room, Brad's first day. Charlie Dixon was a good band. Charlie Dixon was a good band. In fact, if it, uh, in fact if it wasn't for him, uh, I think Troy's family had broken up on one time for a year.
But, did he record with anybody or other than Troy?
